title: Horizon Quantum Reports Q2 2026 Financial Results: Warrant Cash Infusion, Beryllium Early Access, and European Testbed Expansion - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Horizon Quantum Holdings (NASDAQ: HQ), fresh off a March 2026 SPAC merger with dMY Squared, closed Q2 2026 with $113.25M cash after $27.5M of public warrant exercises, zero revenue, and a headline ($115.23M) net loss that is almost entirely a $108.29M non-cash mark-to-market charge on warrant derivative liabilities triggered by a rising stock price. Operationally it shipped its Beryllium quantum programming language to early access, opened the Ember-1 superconducting testbed in Singapore, and confirmed a 256-qubit IonQ trapped-ion system for a Dublin second testbed.

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum Holdings (NASDAQ: HQ) took in $27.5 million of gross proceeds during Q2 2026 from the exercise of 2.4 million publicly traded warrants under the ticker HQWWW, funding the company without a dilutive follow-on equity raise.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Warrant exercises are the de facto financing channel for this post-SPAC name; the pace of exercises, not revenue, is the near-term cash driver to track.
insights.quote: The company received $27.5 million in gross proceeds from the exercise of 2.4 million publicly traded warrants (HQWWW) during Q2.
insights.locator: Financial Results and Warrant Cash Infusion

insights.claim: As of August 3, 2026 roughly 2.5 million Horizon Quantum public warrants had been exercised, representing 79% of total outstanding public warrants and cumulative gross proceeds of $28.7 million, meaning only about a fifth of the warrant funding pool remains untapped.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The residual warrant overhang is small, so the incremental cash left from this source is capped near $7-8M — the next raise will likely have to be a real equity or debt event.
insights.quote: total warrant exercises reached approximately 2.5 million (79% of total outstanding public warrants), bringing cumulative gross proceeds to $28.7 million
insights.locator: Subsequent to quarter-end, as of August 3

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum ended June 30, 2026 with $113.25 million in cash and cash equivalents, up $16.65 million sequentially from $96.60 million and up from just $0.71 million a year earlier — a roughly 15,900% year-over-year increase driven by the SPAC and warrant proceeds rather than operations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Against a ($5.46M) quarterly adjusted EBITDA burn, that cash stack implies multiple years of runway, removing near-term financing risk as a bear case.
insights.locator: This cash inflow elevated total cash

insights.claim: The pre-merger entity Horizon Quantum Computing Pte. Ltd. held only $0.71 million of cash in Q2 2025, so the SPAC merger with dMY Squared Technology Group completed on March 19, 2026 is what converted a cash-starved startup into a $113 million balance sheet.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Year-over-year comparisons for this name are structurally meaningless; only post-March-2026 periods reflect the fundable business.
insights.locator: Because the company completed its SPAC merger

themes.theme: Optical Net Loss vs Real Burn

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum's reported GAAP net loss of ($115.23) million in Q2 2026, or ($2.20) per ordinary share, was driven by a $108.29 million non-cash mark-to-market remeasurement of warrant-related derivative liabilities caused by the stock price rising during the quarter, not by operating deterioration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Screeners and headline-driven sellers will read a 3,873% YoY loss explosion; the charge is an artifact of share-price strength and reverses in direction if the stock falls.
insights.quote: a $108.29 million non-cash accounting charge resulting from the mark-to-market fair value remeasurement of warrant-related derivative liabilities, caused by an increase in Horizon’s stock price during the quarter
insights.locator: Reported GAAP Net Loss for Q2 2026

insights.claim: A rising share price mechanically increases the reported loss at post-SPAC companies carrying warrant derivative liabilities, creating a perverse relationship where good stock performance produces worse GAAP earnings while cash is untouched.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Apply the same adjustment lens to every de-SPAC in the quantum and deep-tech cohort before treating a loss spike as a fundamental signal.
insights.quote: This charge had no impact on cash balances or operations.
insights.locator: This charge had no impact on cash

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum's Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss was ($5.46) million versus ($2.06) million in Q2 2025 once the non-cash derivative adjustment, share-based compensation, and non-recurring public transition costs are excluded — roughly 2.6x higher underlying burn year over year.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This ~$5.5M/quarter figure, not the $115M headline, is the number to model runway and future raises against.
insights.locator: On a non-GAAP basis, excluding the non-cash

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum's operating expenses reached $7.18 million in Q2 2026, up 10.5% sequentially and 158.3% year over year, driven by expanded R&D headcount and newly required public-company compliance infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sequential opex growth of ~10% per quarter compounds fast; if sustained it roughly halves the implied runway within two years absent new funding.
insights.locator: Total operating expenses rose to $7.18 million

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum booked $0.00 in revenue in both Q2 2026 and Q1 2026 versus $0.04 million in Q2 2025, a 100% year-over-year decline that leaves the company entirely pre-commercial.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: There is no revenue line to value; the equity is a pure option on the Beryllium/Triple Alpha software stack converting early-access users into paying customers.
insights.locator: Amounts in $M Q2’2026 Q1’2026 Q2’2025 Revenue

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum released Beryllium, a high-level object-oriented quantum programming language, to early access users at the end of Q2 2026, targeting classical software engineers with familiar constructs such as classes, functions, and libraries inside quantum workflows.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Developer adoption of a proprietary language is the company's only plausible moat and the first observable leading indicator ahead of revenue.

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum is building a three-tier compiler stack in which Beryllium compiles down to Helium, a BASIC-like intermediate language, and then to Hydrogen, an assembly language, deliberately hiding low-level quantum mechanics from application developers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The bet is that quantum value accrues to the abstraction layer rather than the qubit, mirroring how CUDA rather than transistors captured AI compute economics.
insights.quote: Beryllium compiles down to Helium (a BASIC-like language) and Hydrogen (assembly language) to abstract away low-level quantum mechanics for developers
insights.locator: Designed to enable modern classical software engineering constructs

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum's first testbed, Ember-1, is a superconducting system at its Singapore headquarters that opened to select early users in Q2 2026 and is integrated directly with the Triple Alpha platform to give pulse- and gate-level access with real-time execution of complete quantum programs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Owning local hardware rather than renting cloud qubits is a cost and control decision that shows up as capex and opex growth well before any revenue.
insights.quote: bypassing latency issues associated with remote cloud execution

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum purchased a 256-qubit trapped-ion system from IonQ in June 2026 to serve as its second testbed at a new European headquarters in Dublin, Ireland, deliberately spanning both solid-state and atom-based architectures.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IonQ gains a disclosed hardware customer while Horizon signals modality-agnostic software positioning — a hedge that pays off whichever qubit technology wins.
insights.quote: giving the company a multi-modality testbed across both solid-state and atom-based architectures

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum is establishing a European headquarters in Dublin alongside its Singapore base, giving the company a two-jurisdiction footprint spanning Asian and EU quantum funding and procurement programs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Physical EU presence is often a prerequisite for sovereign quantum contracts, so watch for European public-sector awards as the first revenue channel.
insights.locator: will be located at its European headquarters

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum and Quantum Machines announced a strategic collaboration in July 2026 to co-develop an embedded calibration framework for Ember-1, embedding lightweight continuous calibration routines into normal system operation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Control-electronics vendors like Quantum Machines are quietly becoming the picks-and-shovels layer as every quantum operator confronts the same calibration problem.

insights.claim: Lengthy full-system calibration halts are treated as the limiting factor on quantum system availability, and eliminating them via continuous embedded calibration is framed as the path to maximizing uptime.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Effective machine-hours, not raw qubit counts, may become the real commercial metric for quantum hardware — a useful screen for comparing operators.
insights.quote: maximize system uptime and eliminate the need for lengthy full-system calibration halts
insights.locator: By integrating lightweight, continuous calibration routines
